filing-20260807-5220.point: CEBA says abeyance lets SPP and stakeholders work collaboratively instead of moving the debate to the FERC docket.
filing-20260807-5220.quote: as opposed to a rushed proposal that would unnecessarily shift stakeholder debate to the Commission docket.

filing-20260807-5220.point: CEBA says the abeyance accommodates the Regional State Committee and SPP Board meetings.
filing-20260807-5220.quote: reasonable accommodations necessary to convene the Regional State Committee and the SPP Board of Directors

filing-20260807-5220.point: CEBA says the 95 days would not materially slow reform and would improve commercial viability and legal durability.
filing-20260807-5220.quote: extension would not materially impede the Commission's objectives for advancing reforms quickly yet offers significant benefits

filing-20260807-5150.point: Missouri PSC says the 95 days fits SPP's November 17 Board meeting and state input to the compliance filing.
filing-20260807-5150.quote: SPP's Board of Directors meeting is scheduled for November 17, 2026—one day outside the 90-day window.

filing-20260807-5150.point: It cites the 12-month Order No. 1920 extension FERC gave SPP in April 2025 as precedent for good cause.
filing-20260807-5150.quote: the Commission granted SPP a 12-month extension of time to submit filings in compliance with the Commission's Order No. 1920

filing-20260807-5150.point: State regulators care about transparency and cost-shift avoidance because they set retail rates that include transmission costs.
filing-20260807-5150.quote: Issues related to transparency and the avoidance of cost shifting are particularly important to the Missouri PSC and other state regulators who bear the responsibility of setting retail rates

filing-20260807-5150.point: The abeyance gives the CARE Team time to finish cost mitigation recommendations for the Board.
filing-20260807-5150.quote: The requested abeyance will allow the CARE Team time to complete this important work and present its recommendations to the Board.

filing-20260807-5123.point: The RSC says cost allocation for large loads falls within its regional governance role.
filing-20260807-5123.quote: These issues directly implicate the RSC's responsibility within the SPP regional governance structure for determining regional proposals concerning the allocation of transmission costs.

filing-20260807-5123.point: The CARE Team is evaluating how to assign or secure costs when projected large load does not materialize or stay.
filing-20260807-5123.quote: particularly when projected load does not materialize as anticipated or does not remain on the system for the period used to justify transmission investment.

filing-20260807-5123.point: The CARE Team expects to bring a recommendation to the RSC and SPP Board on November 16 and 17, 2026.
filing-20260807-5123.quote: quarterly business meetings on November 16 and 17, 2026.

filing-20260807-5123.point: The RSC says the extra time is not unnecessary delay.
filing-20260807-5123.quote: The RSC recognizes the urgency of addressing the challenges presented by rapid large-load growth and does not seek unnecessary delay.

motion-el26-68-spp-abeyance.point: Joint Movants ask for 95 days, five more than the order contemplates, to fit SPP's Board meeting.
motion-el26-68-spp-abeyance.quote: The additional five (5) days is necessary to accommodate SPP's full stakeholder process, which culminates in a scheduled Board of Directors

motion-el26-68-spp-abeyance.point: SPP will add alternative transmission technology evaluation to its HILL study process, which does not now require it.
motion-el26-68-spp-abeyance.quote: it does not currently require SPP to evaluate alternative transmission technologies when studying HILLs.

motion-el26-68-spp-abeyance.point: SPP will revise pro forma NITS and point-to-point service agreements to carry HILL operational requirements.
motion-el26-68-spp-abeyance.quote: to develop revisions to the Tariff's pro forma transmission service agreements

motion-el26-68-spp-abeyance.point: The CARE Team is weighing financial security, direct assignment of upgrade costs and minimum contributions from customers serving large loads.
motion-el26-68-spp-abeyance.quote: direct assignment, in whole or in part, of Network Upgrade costs associated with large load delivery point additions or modifications

motion-el26-68-spp-abeyance.point: On co-location and behind-the-meter generation, stakeholders must settle terminology, the study process and overlap among transmission, interconnection and market registration.
motion-el26-68-spp-abeyance.quote: the overlap between transmission service, interconnection, and market registration requirements.

motion-el26-68-spp-abeyance.point: Price Adaptive Load Service would create non-firm service with usage-based pricing and mandatory dispatchability.
motion-el26-68-spp-abeyance.quote: PALS would establish a new transmission service under which participating loads would receive transmission service subject to usage-based pricing, mandatory dispatchability requirements

motion-el26-68-spp-abeyance.point: Working group votes run September and October, MOPC in October, RSC in November, and the Board on November 17, 2026.
motion-el26-68-spp-abeyance.quote: culminating in working group votes during September and October, MOPC in October, the RSC where applicable in November, and final Board consideration on November 17, 2026.

filing-20260722-5143.point: SPP says the motion conflicts with the show cause orders' tailoring to each region.
filing-20260722-5143.quote: Because of the vast regional differences in such things as cost allocation, cost transparency, study processes, network upgrades, and market operations, it would be impossible to resolve all the issues presented by the Commission in the Show Cause Orders in a single settlement proceeding.

filing-20260722-5143.point: SPP supports the SPP TO Group's answer that the motion is premature.
filing-20260722-5143.quote: SPP supports the SPP TO Group Answer in its request for the Commission to deny the Marlowe Motion as being premature

filing-20260722-5143.point: SPP argues no controversy exists yet because no tariff revisions or record exist.
filing-20260722-5143.quote: Because no proposed tariff revisions have been filed and no administrative record has been developed, there is presently no concrete controversy suitable for settlement.

filing-20260722-5143.point: SPP says the movant's own framework can be presented through ordinary comment and stakeholder processes.
filing-20260722-5143.quote: those matters may be presented through the ordinary comment and stakeholder processes available in these proceedings.

report-el26-68-spp.point: SPP lists complementary initiatives it says have improved planning, resource addition and large load integration.
report-el26-68-spp.quote: SPP has developed complementary initiatives that improve planning certainty, accelerate the addition of new resources, enhance operational flexibility, strengthen resource adequacy accountability

report-el26-68-spp.point: SPP's East balancing area shows a 17.1 percent summer 2026 reserve margin, about 5,752 MW above requirements.
report-el26-68-spp.quote: the East BAA maintains a reserve margin of 17.1%, representing approximately 5,752 MW of excess accredited capacity above the total RAR.

report-el26-68-spp.point: At the ERAS filing SPP predicted a 2-3 GW accredited capacity shortfall by 2030.
report-el26-68-spp.quote: SPP predicted that the SPP Region could face a 2-3 GW accredited capacity shortfall by 2030.

report-el26-68-spp.point: ERAS has 36 active requests representing about 13.3 GW, with none withdrawn.
report-el26-68-spp.quote: there are 36 active ERAS requests representing approximately 13.3 GW of generating capacity and no requests have withdrawn.

report-el26-68-spp.point: SPP defines HILLs at 10 MW or more at 69 kV and below, or 50 MW or more above 69 kV.
report-el26-68-spp.quote: 50 MW or more if connected to the Transmission System at a voltage level greater than 69 kV

report-el26-68-spp.point: PALS would be a non-firm service with usage-based billing for fully dispatchable loads subject to curtailment.
report-el26-68-spp.quote: PALS would utilize a usage-based billing structure and require participating loads to be fully dispatchable

report-el26-68-spp.point: PAL/PALS faces MOPC and RSC votes on October 13 and November 16, with a FERC filing by November 16, 2026.
report-el26-68-spp.quote: final votes by MOPC on October 13, 2026, and the RSC on November 16, 2026.

filing-20260715-5116.point: The TO Group calls the motion premature and disruptive to FERC's choice of regional show cause proceedings.
filing-20260715-5116.quote: The Commission should deny the Motion because it is premature and would profoundly disrupt the Commission's well-reasoned decision to address the challenge of large load additions on a regional basis

filing-20260715-5116.point: A nationwide settlement would reject FERC's choice of regional solutions developed through stakeholder processes.
filing-20260715-5116.quote: it is a rejection of the Commission's pointed choice to address large load issues on a regional basis, rather than impose a rigid nationwide rule

filing-20260715-5116.point: Hundreds of ANOPR commenters would face cost and logistics in a Commission-run settlement.
filing-20260715-5116.quote: Hundreds of parties have submitted comments in response to the ANOPR, the overwhelming majority of whom are located outside of Washington, D.C.

filing-20260715-5116.point: The 90-day abeyance option in the show cause orders already provides for stakeholder cooperation.
filing-20260715-5116.quote: Orders already provide for the exact cooperation Movant claims to seek, without the extra administrative burden.

filing-20260715-5116.point: The movant's interest rests on a claimed framework, and she alleges no concrete injury from the interlocutory orders.
filing-20260715-5116.quote: The Movant alleges no cognizable, concrete, or particularized injury from the Commission's interlocutory Show Cause Orders
